newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Gdansk to issue PLN 10.7 mln bonds.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Gdansk to issue PLN 10.7 mln bonds.

text.p: The Polish city of Gdansk will issue this year 10.7 million zlotys worth of floating rate municipal bonds as the first tranche of a 99.3 million zloty borrowing, the city's mayor said on Friday.
Tomasz Posadzki told a news conference the issue would be broken down into six tranches issued between 1996 and 1998.

Gdansk chose a consortium of Poland's Bank Gdanski SA, Bank Handlowy and Merrill Lynch International to lead the issue last March and Posadzki was speaking after the signing of an official agreement with the institutions.
Under the agreement, Gdanski and Handlowy would place two-thirds of the issue on the domestic market and Merrill Lynch would offer the rest internationally.
Posadzki said next year Gdansk planned three bond issues worth 56 million zlotys and two tranches in 1998 worth 36.2 million zlotys.
Gdansk would redeem the bonds no sooner than January 1, 2000 and not later than the end of 2004.

One-year bonds would carry an annual coupon at 50 basis points above the average yield of 52-week T-bills auctioned at two primary auctions preceding the issue and each coupoTwo-year paper would carry a 70 b.p. premium, three-year bonmd a 100 b.p. premium and the four-year and five-year bond a 105 b.p. premium.
